_comment: Canonical Chinese renderings. Add a term here the moment you settle on a wording, so the choice sticks. `banned` is matched as a plain substring against the text this patch ships: data/tl_trans.json. A variant that is also an ordinary Chinese word, or a fragment of another name, cannot be banned -- pin it with a note here instead.

Alicia._note: The original says Alicia, not Alice. The translation shipped inside archive.rpa renders it 爱丽丝; zz_zh_locale.rpy overrides that at runtime, and this entry is what stops a later pass from putting 爱丽丝 back into the dialogue database.

???._note: The three-way speaker the game never names. Full-width question marks, no speaker prefix.

The Council._note: 委员会 cannot be banned here even though it is what a lazy pass would write for The Council: the script also says "file a complaint ... through the commission", where 委员会 is correct. 评议委员会 is the shape worth catching.

IntervAI._note: A proper noun that stays in Latin script; the game never writes it out.

_banned_is_a_blunt_substring_match: None of the variants above is an ordinary Chinese word, so a plain substring match is enough. 娜米/纳米 and 两人/俩个人 are the two closest calls: 纳米 is a real word (nanometre) and this game's text never mentions one, but if that ever changes the entry has to go.
